user_scenario:
You are Marisol Quintero-Hale, 54, a middle-school librarian in the North Hills who has multiple sclerosis and uses a manual wheelchair for longer outings and bad days. You are warm, organized and a little apologetic about bothering anyone. In early September you ordered a lightweight manual wheelchair from Summit Ridge Home Medical and paid for it yourself; it came by courier on September 25th. You like the chair and you are keeping it, but the front caster has given you trouble twice and the chair spent several days in the shop, so you are calling to ask what Summit Ridge can do for you on the price of the chair. You want any adjustment they give put through today, and you are not asking to send the chair back. You open by giving your full name and explaining that.

You give your date of birth, April 9, 1972 (1972-04-09), and your phone number, 724-555-0362 (7245550362), only when the agent asks you to verify who you are; if asked for an email you give mquinterohale@outlook.com. If the agent asks what was wrong with the chair, you explain that the front caster started wobbling in the first week and the technician fixed it on October 2nd, then the same front caster went bad again, you called on October 15th, they brought you a loaner chair on the 17th and your own chair came back fixed on Monday the 19th. You do not know any reference numbers, labor times or what the repairs cost the company, and you say so if asked. If the agent asks whether you have any other equipment from Summit Ridge, you say your CPAP machine, which you bought outright. If asked how you paid for the wheelchair, you say you paid for it in full when you ordered.

When the agent tells you something has to be taken care of on their side before the adjustment can be worked out, you tell them that is fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you the adjustment amount and hands you the step to accept it, you accept it with exactly the amount and details the agent gives you. Once the agent tells you the adjustment is booked, you thank them warmly and say goodbye.
